headline: Approved $340,000 CBIZ audit contract, adopted $1,607,694.55 budget supplement, and passed ordinances on stop signs, secondhand dealers, and comment time
summary: The board approved a two-year, $340,000 audit contract with CBIZ CPAS, P.C., and adopted a $1,607,694.55 supplemental budget appropriation (R-26-048) in seven separate line-item votes covering playground equipment, a dental program, retirements, and COVID expenses. It gave final passage to ordinances on a Pinebrook Road stop sign, secondhand dealer definitions, and expanded public comment time, tabled R-26-049 (a Homeless Services Gap Analysis Committee), and referred several new resolutions and an ordinance on sewer fees to committee.
decisions: Approved a two-year contract with CBIZ CPAS, P.C. for up to $340,000 covering FY26 and FY27 audits.
Approved David Campbell's request to unmerge two lots, Parcel 89-21, that were involuntarily merged by the City.
Approved $2,500 from the Nashua Arts Commission to support the Arts City Project run by Nashua Artist Quest Nine (Kori Thomas).
Approved the petition for issuance of building permits for Silver Lining Development, LLC, Map 129, Lots 187 & 259.
Referred the Mayor's reappointment of Joseph Duquette to the Airport Authority to the Personnel/Administrative Affairs Committee.
Gave final passage to R-26-046, authorizing the sale of surplus property.
Approved Line Item A of R-26-048 for $247,386.18 for Ledge Street playground equipment, 14-0.
Approved a line item of R-26-048 for $100,000 for the dental program, Traveling Tooth Fairies, 14-0.
Approved Line Item C of R-26-048 for $500,000.00 to fund upcoming city retirements, 13-1.
Approved Line Item E of R-26-048 for $5,250.00 for park and field rehabilitation, 14-0.
Approved Line Item F of R-26-048 for $42,758.50 for park and field rehabilitation, 14-0.
Approved Line Item G of R-26-048 for $672,299.87 to cover salary and wage expenses during COVID-19, 13-1.
Approved Line Item D of R-26-048 for $40,000 for salaries and non-salary expenses for the Lead Grant activity, 11-3.
Adopted Resolution R-26-048, the $1,607,694.55 supplemental appropriation, after passing it in seven separate line items.
Tabled R-26-049, which would have established a Homeless Services Gap Analysis Committee.
Gave final passage to R-26-050, transferring $35,000 to fund the Nashua Association for the Elderly.
Gave final passage to R-26-051, relative to auctioning tax deeded property.
Confirmed Michael McDowell's appointment to the Arts Commission, with a term to expire June 9, 2029.
Amended and gave final passage to O-26-012, amending the definition of secondhand dealers.
Gave final passage to O-26-016, authorizing a stop sign on Pinebrook Road at its intersection with Ridge Road.
Gave final passage to O-26-017, removing the language for a solid waste equipment reserve fund and discontinuing the fund.
Gave final passage to O-26-018, removing the total time limit for public comment periods during committee meetings.
Gave final passage to O-26-019, incorporating the Environmental Health Department subdivision review fee with other subdivision plan review fees.
Rejected a motion to re-refer O-26-020, on overnight parking in Ward 5, back to committee.
Approved indefinite postponement of O-26-020, on overnight on-street parking in Ward 5 from May 1st to October 31st.
Rejected a motion to amend O-26-021 by replacing it with the Personnel/Administrative Affairs Committee's golden rod copy.
Approved amending O-26-021 to allow each speaker 3 minutes 30 seconds during the first public comment period and 3 minutes during the second.
Gave final passage to O-26-021 as amended, increasing individual public comment time during the first public comment period, 11-3.
Gave R-26-053 its first reading, assigned it to the Budget Review Committee, and scheduled a public hearing for August 24, 2026.
Gave R-26-054, authorizing Pennichuck Corporation to renew its TD Bank line of credit, its first reading and assigned it to the Pennichuck Water Special Committee.
Gave R-26-055 its first reading and assigned it to the Budget Review Committee.
Gave R-26-056 its first reading and assigned it to the Budget Review Committee.
Gave O-26-023, increasing sewer use fee rates and charges, its first reading and assigned it to the Personnel/Administrative Affairs Committee and Board of Public Works.

By the Numbers
Greenhouse gas (GHG) inventories calculate, quantify, and assess community associated emissions and their sources.
Municipalities like Nashua conduct GHG inventories to:
Identify sources of emissions, targeting efficiency projects
Demonstrate transparency
Act as climate action leaders
Measure progress towards local, state, federal, and international climate goals 
Secure funding and grants, some of which require GHG inventories
Join a growing network of municipalities dedicated to sustainability 
Provide residents with a comprehensive view of local emissions, driving decision making
